blueprints.title: Work out powers
blueprints.author: OpenPath (written with AI assistance; not educator-reviewed)

chapter.title: A power is repeated multiplication
text: 2⁵ means 2 multiplied by itself 5 times. The small raised number (the power) counts how many 2s there are; it is not a number to multiply by.

screens.title: Count them out
text: Write the number as many times as the power says, with × between them. Then multiply two at a time.

strategies.title: Build it up one step at a time

screens.title: Multiply again and again
text: Start with the number and multiply by it again for each extra power. That is one multiplication fewer than the power.

strategies.title: Use the multiplication facts you know

screens.title: Each step is a fact
text: Every step of a power is a multiplication fact: 2 × 2 = 4, 4 × 2 = 8, 8 × 2 = 16. If a step is slow, say that times table first.

blueprints.title: Expand a bracket: a(x + b)
blueprints.author: OpenPath (written with AI assistance; not educator-reviewed)

chapter.title: The number outside multiplies everything inside
text: 3(x + 4) means three lots of (x + 4): (x + 4) + (x + 4) + (x + 4). That is three x's and three 4s.
chapter.tip: Multiply every term in the bracket, not only the first one.

screens.title: Split the rectangle
text: Draw a rectangle a high and x + b long. Split the long side into x and b. The two parts have areas a × x and a × b; together they are the whole rectangle.

screens.title: Multiply along each arrow
text: Draw an arrow from the number outside the bracket to each term inside it, and multiply along each arrow.

screens.title: The last term is a fact
text: The number at the end is the number outside times the number inside: 3 × 4 = 12. If that fact is slow, rebuild it from one you know: 3 × 4 is 3 × 2 doubled.

blueprints.title: Expand (x + a)(x + b)
blueprints.author: OpenPath (written with AI assistance; not educator-reviewed)

chapter.title: Four products
text: In (x + 2)(x + 5), each term of the first bracket multiplies each term of the second: x × x, x × 5, 2 × x and 2 × 5.
chapter.tip: The x term is the SUM of the two numbers; the last term is their PRODUCT.

screens.title: Fill the four cells
text: Draw a 2 by 2 grid. Write x and a along the top, x and b down the side. Fill each cell with the product of its row and column, then add the two cells that have an x.

screens.title: Two of the four products have an x
text: Multiply the first terms, the outer terms, the inner terms and the last terms. The outer and inner products are the two x terms: add them.

screens.title: Keep each sign
text: When a number is negative, keep its sign in each product. The x term is the sum of the two signed products, so a negative product makes it smaller.

blueprints.title: Differentiate powers of x
blueprints.author: OpenPath (written with AI assistance; not educator-reviewed)

chapter.title: The power rule
text: To differentiate k xⁿ, bring the power down as a factor and lower the power by one: the derivative is k n xⁿ⁻¹. Then put in the value of x.
chapter.tip: Lower the power first, then substitute.

strategies.title: A derivative is a rate of change

screens.title: Not the value: how fast it changes
text: f′(3) is how fast f is changing at x = 3, not the value f(3). For f(x) = x², the values at 2.9, 3 and 3.1 are 8.41, 9 and 9.61: they rise by 1.2 over 0.2, which is 6 per unit, and the rule gives 2 × 3 = 6.

screens.title: In this order
text: Multiply the coefficient by the power, then take one off the power. Only then put in the number.

screens.title: A power is repeated multiplication
text: 2² = 2 × 2 = 4 and 2³ = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8. A power is not the number times the power: 2³ is not 6.

blueprints.title: Integrate powers of x
blueprints.author: OpenPath (written with AI assistance; not educator-reviewed)

chapter.title: Reverse the power rule
text: Differentiating xⁿ⁺¹ ⁄ (n + 1) gives xⁿ. So an antiderivative of k xⁿ is k xⁿ⁺¹ ⁄ (n + 1): raise the power by one, then divide by the new power.
math: ∫ k xⁿ dx = k xⁿ⁺¹ ⁄ (n + 1) + C

chapter.title: Between two limits
text: For a definite integral, work out the antiderivative F at the upper limit and at the lower limit, then subtract: F(upper) − F(lower). The constant C cancels.

screens.title: Undo, then check
text: Whatever antiderivative you write, differentiate it: you must get back the function you started with. x³ differentiates to 3x², so ∫ 3x² dx = x³ + C.

screens.title: Two moves, then the limits
text: Add one to the power, then divide by that new power. Then put in the upper limit and the lower limit, and subtract.

screens.title: What the working needs
text: The working needs powers (2³ = 8) and fractions with the same denominator (16⁄3 − 2⁄3 = 14⁄3). If either is slow, practise it first; the integration itself is two moves.

blueprints.title: Integrate by substitution
blueprints.author: OpenPath (written with AI assistance; not educator-reviewed)

chapter.title: Spot u and du
text: In ∫ 2x(x² + 1)² dx, call the inside of the bracket u = x² + 1. Its derivative, 2x, is already there: du = 2x dx. So the integral is ∫ u² du.

chapter.title: Change the limits
text: With limits, change them too: put each x limit into u = x² + 1, and integrate between those u values. You never go back to x.
chapter.tip: Using the x limits for u is the most common slip.

screens.title: Nothing left to divide by
text: du ⁄ dx = 2x, so a small change dx in x changes u by 2x dx. The 2x in the integral is exactly what turns dx into du: there is no extra 2 to divide by.

strategies.title: Make a little table of limits

screens.title: x row, u row
text: Write two rows, x and u. Under x put the two limits; under u put x² + c for each. Then integrate in u between the u values.

screens.title: The last step is arithmetic
text: The last step is powers of whole numbers, like 2³ = 8 and 5³ = 125, then a subtraction and a division. A power is repeated multiplication, not the number times the power.

blueprints.title: How many solutions? The discriminant
blueprints.author: OpenPath (written with AI assistance; not educator-reviewed)

chapter.title: b² − 4ac decides
text: For ax² + bx + c = 0, work out the discriminant b² − 4ac. Positive: two different real solutions. Zero: one (repeated) solution. Negative: no real solutions.
chapter.tip: b² is never negative, even when b is.

screens.title: Crossings
text: y = x² + bx + c is a U-shaped curve. Two solutions: it crosses the x-axis twice. One: it just touches it. None: it stays above it. The discriminant tells you which, without drawing.

strategies.title: Write each part with its sign

screens.title: b², then 4ac, then subtract
text: Write b², then 4ac with c's own sign, then subtract.

screens.title: Two sign facts
text: Taking away a negative number adds: 16 − (−20) = 36. And a square is never negative: (−4)² = 16.
